title: backdrop-filter: blur() - Filters - Tailwind CSS
content_text:
FILTERS backdrop-filter: blur() Utilities for applying backdrop blur filters to an element. Class Styles backdrop-blur-xs backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-xs)); /* 4px */ backdrop-blur-sm backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-sm)); /* 8px */ backdrop-blur-md backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-md)); /* 12px */ backdrop-blur-lg backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-lg)); /* 16px */ backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-xl)); /* 24px */ backdrop-blur-2xl backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-2xl)); /* 40px */ backdrop-blur-3xl backdrop-filter: blur(var(--blur-3xl)); /* 64px */ backdrop-blur-none backdrop-filter: ; backdrop-blur-() backdrop-filter: blur(var()); backdrop-blur-[] backdrop-filter: blur(); EXAMPLES Basic example Use utilities like backdrop-blur-sm and backdrop-blur-lg to control an element’s backdrop blur: backdrop-blur-none backdrop-blur-sm backdrop-blur-md
Using a custom value Use the backdrop-blur-[] syntax to set the backdrop blur based on a completely custom value:
For CSS variables, you can also use the backdrop-blur-() syntax:
This is just a shorthand for backdrop-blur-[var()] that adds the var() function for you automatically. Responsive design Prefix a backdrop-filter: blur() utility with a breakpoint variant like md: to only apply the utility at medium screen sizes and above:
Learn more about using variants in the variants documentation. Customizing your theme Use the --blur-* theme variables to customize the backdrop blur utilities in your project: @theme { --blur-2xs: 2px; } Now the backdrop-blur-2xs utility can be used in your markup:
Learn more about customizing your theme in the theme documentation. backdrop-filter brightness
